title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Education on Issuing the Opinions on Implementing the System of Occupational Prohibition
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, and Ministry of Education

Notice on Printing and Distributing the Opinions on Implementing the Employment Prohibition System

Fa Fa [2022] No. 32

The Higher People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and Education Departments (Commissions) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, and the Education Bureau:

In order to strictly implement the employment prohibition system for persons with criminal records, purify the campus environment, and protect minors, in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law, the Law on the Protection of Minors, the Teachers Law, and other legal provisions, and in light of the circumstances reflected in law enforcement and judicial practice, the Supreme People's Court, together with the Supreme People's Procuratorate and the Ministry of Education, has formulated the Opinions on Implementing the Employment Prohibition System. The Opinions are hereby printed and distributed, and all parties are requested to conscientiously implement them in light of actual conditions. If any issues arise during implementation, please report them promptly to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Education, respectively.

November 10, 2022

Opinions on Implementing the Employment Prohibition System

In order to implement the system of inquiry into the criminal records of faculty and staff of schools, kindergartens, and other educational institutions as well as off-campus training institutions, strictly implement the employment prohibition system for persons with criminal records, purify the campus environment, and effectively protect minors, in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law), the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors (hereinafter referred to as the Law on the Protection of Minors), the Teachers Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Teachers Law), and other legal provisions, the following opinions are proposed:

1. In accordance with the provisions of Article 37 bis, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, where a faculty or staff member commits a crime by taking advantage of professional convenience, or commits a crime that violates specific duties required by the profession and is sentenced to a criminal penalty, the People's Court may, based on the circumstances of the crime and the need to prevent recidivism, prohibit the person from engaging in related professions for a specified period. If other laws or administrative regulations contain other prohibitive or restrictive provisions on the person's engagement in related professions, such provisions shall prevail.

The Law on the Protection of Minors and the Teachers Law are laws within the meaning of the preceding paragraph, and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications are administrative regulations within the meaning of the preceding paragraph.

2. In accordance with the provisions of Article 62 of the Law on the Protection of Minors, persons who have committed illegal or criminal acts such as sexual assault, abuse, trafficking, or violent injury are prohibited from engaging in work involving close contact with minors.

In accordance with the provisions of Article 14 of the Teachers Law and Article 18 of the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications, a person who has been deprived of political rights or has been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment or a heavier penalty for an intentional crime cannot obtain teacher qualifications; if teacher qualifications have already been obtained, they are forfeited, and the person cannot re-obtain teacher qualifications.

3. Where a faculty or staff member commits a crime such as sexual assault, abuse, trafficking, or violent injury, the People's Court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 62 of the Law on the Protection of Minors, sentence the person to be prohibited from engaging in work involving close contact with minors.

Where a faculty or staff member commits a crime other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court may, based on the circumstances of the crime and the need to prevent recidivism, in accordance with the provisions of Article 37 bis, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, sentence the person to be prohibited from engaging in related professions for a period of three to five years, calculated from the date of completion of the criminal penalty or the date of parole; or, in accordance with the provisions of Article 38, paragraph 2 and Article 72, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law, apply a prohibition order to the person.

4. Where it is necessary to prohibit a faculty or staff member from engaging in related professions or to apply a prohibition order, the People's Procuratorate shall, when initiating a public prosecution, make corresponding recommendations.

5. For criminal cases involving crimes committed by faculty or staff members, after the judgment becomes effective, the People's Court shall, within thirty days, serve the judgment document on the education administrative department at the location of the defendant's unit; where necessary, the education administrative department shall forward the judgment document to the relevant competent department.

Where it is inappropriate to serve the judgment document due to reasons such as involving the privacy of a minor, relevant evidentiary materials containing the defendant's personal information, charge, and term of imprisonment may be served instead.

6. After the judgment rendered by the People's Court in a case involving a crime committed by a faculty or staff member becomes effective, the unit to which the person belongs, the education administrative department, or the relevant competent department may, in accordance with the Law on the Protection of Minors, the Teachers Law, the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications, and other laws and regulations, impose corresponding sanctions, disciplinary actions, or penalties.

Where the circumstances meet the conditions for forfeiture of teacher qualifications or revocation of teacher qualifications, the education administrative department shall promptly confiscate the person's teacher qualification certificate.

7. The People's Procuratorate shall supervise the implementation of the employment prohibition and prohibition orders.

8. Where a People's Court or a People's Procuratorate discovers that a relevant unit has failed to implement the system of inquiry into criminal records or the employment prohibition system, it shall make recommendations to that unit.

9. For the purposes of these Opinions, "faculty and staff members" refers to teachers, teaching support personnel, administrative personnel, service personnel, security personnel working in schools, kindergartens, and other educational institutions, as well as relevant staff of off-campus training institutions.

Where the sponsors or actual controllers of schools, kindergartens, and other educational institutions, or off-campus training institutions commit crimes, these Opinions shall apply mutatis mutandis.

10. These Opinions shall take effect as of November 15, 2022.
